headlines.title: SDR reply rate falls 51% from the first two steps to step 7 and beyond
headlines.detail: Early steps reply at 6.41%, late steps at 3.12%, with no interval overlap. Early steps are mostly inbound_ack (6.41%). At late steps no theme clears the volume and cadence-diversity bar, so there is no copy swap to recommend: the decay looks structural, not a framing choice.
headlines.action: 5,377 late-step sends earned 168 replies. Question whether those steps should exist before rewriting them. Cutting the tail is the lever here, not new copy.

headlines.title: BDR-Strategic replies 2.4x better than BDR-Velocity, and 15% of it is which themes they run
headlines.detail: BDR-Strategic runs at 1.54% and BDR-Velocity at 0.65%. The concrete difference in the copy: BDR-Strategic puts 37% of its volume into peer_proof against 9% for BDR-Velocity; BDR-Velocity puts 28% of its volume into risk_trust, which replies at 0.32% for them, while BDR-Strategic does not use it at all. Re-weighting BDR-Velocity to BDR-Strategic's theme mix would take it to 0.82%, which is about 15% of the gap. The rest is audience or execution, not which themes are used.
headlines.action: Move BDR-Velocity's risk_trust volume (4,093 sends) into peer_proof. That closes roughly 15% of the gap. Investigate the remaining 85% separately, it is not a copy problem.

headlines.title: BDR reply rate falls 63% from the first two steps to step 7 and beyond

headlines.action: 4,152 late-step sends earned 18 replies. Question whether those steps should exist before rewriting them. Cutting the tail is the lever here, not new copy.
